symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of endogenous variables.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of observed environment slots.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Maximum number of arbitrarily replaced covariance slots.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Set of observed environment labels.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Unknown honest set with \(\lvert H\rvert=h\).

symbols.name: PSDp
symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.name: SPDp
symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-definite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: Observed population covariance family \(\Sigma=(\Sigma_e:e\in E)\), with every observed or replaced slot chosen from the positive-definite covariance domain.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Structural demixing matrix in the equilibrium equation.

symbols.name: H1
symbols.def: Fitted slot set of the first competing BACKSHIFT explanation, with \(\lvert H_1\rvert\ge h\).

symbols.name: H2
symbols.def: Fitted slot set of the second competing BACKSHIFT explanation, with \(\lvert H_2\rvert\ge h\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Overlap \(J=H_1\cap H_2\) of the two fitted slot sets.
symbols.role: Common slots used by the overlap lemma.

symbols.name: D1
symbols.def: Structural matrix \(D^{(1)}\) in the first competing explanation.

symbols.name: D2
symbols.def: Structural matrix \(D^{(2)}\) in the second competing explanation.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Connectivity matrix \(B=I_p-D\).
symbols.role: Causal connectivity target reported by BACKSHIFT.

symbols.name: CP
symbols.def: Maximum absolute product along a directed simple cycle of length at least two.

symbols.name: Dcal
symbols.def: Matrix set satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization defined in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: Invariant disturbance covariance, permitted to be nondiagonal.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Honest intervention-variance levels \(s=(s_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p)\).

symbols.name: s1
symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(1)}=(s^{(1)}_{ek}:e\in H_1,1\le k\le p)\) in the first competing explanation.
symbols.role: First explanation's shifts on the overlap.

symbols.name: s2
symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(2)}=(s^{(2)}_{ek}:e\in H_2,1\le k\le p)\) in the second competing explanation.
symbols.role: Second explanation's shifts on the overlap.

symbols.name: L
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is an affine line in }\mathbb R^2\}\)
symbols.def: Generic affine line used to measure concentration of a pairwise shift cloud.

symbols.name: Mkl
symbols.def: Maximum affine-line occupancy \(M_{k\ell}=\max_L\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Environment deletion distance \(\delta_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}(h-M_{k\ell})\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Proposal-specific prespecified support pattern for shift amplitudes.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Random positive amplitudes indexed by the honest environment and coordinate.

symbols.name: Mgen
symbols.def: Generic occupancy formula \(M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}\).

symbols.name: Rc
symbols.def: Population \(c\)-replacement compatibility set defined in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).
symbols.role: Recovery map for the structural target.

symbols.name: SubsetConsensus
symbols.def: Finite reduction of \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) to exact feasibility-oracle queries over subsets of size \(h\), defined in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\).
symbols.role: Definitional computational interface, not a supplied terminating solver.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Worst-overlap affine-minor separation, equal to zero when \(h-c<3\) and otherwise \(\gamma_H=\min_{k<\ell}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\det[(1,s_{rk},s_{r\ell})_{r\in\{e,f,g\}}]|\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: Condition number \(\kappa_D=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Cycle-product normalization slack \(\zeta_D=1-\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)\).

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Positive-definiteness margin \(\lambda_H=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\Omega),\min_{e\in H}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_e)\}\).

symbols.name: Mbound
symbols.def: Operator-norm scale bound \(M_H=1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Common within-environment sample-size index.
symbols.role: Asymptotic index for the inference layer.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: Calpha
symbols.def: Nonempty simultaneous covariance regions \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{\alpha}=(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}:e\in E)\) at sample-size index \(n\).

symbols.name: rRadius
symbols.def: Honest-slot simultaneous operator-norm radius \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), with value \(+\infty\) allowed.
symbols.role: Observable-region error radius around the honest population covariances.

symbols.name: diamOp
symbols.def: Operator-norm diameter of a nonempty matrix set.
symbols.role: Size of a set-valued structural output.

symbols.name: outerOp
symbols.def: Operator-norm outer radius of a nonempty matrix set around \(D\).
symbols.role: One-sided contraction criterion for the confidence union.

symbols.name: Ualpha
symbols.def: Indexed confidence union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) defined in \(\text{def:confidence-union}\).

symbols.name: gamma0
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound \(\gamma_0\) for the affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H\).

symbols.name: zeta0
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound \(\zeta_0\) for the cycle-product normalization slack \(\zeta_D\).

symbols.name: lambda0
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound \(\lambda_0\) for the positive-definiteness margin \(\lambda_H\).

symbols.name: kappabar
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound \(\overline\kappa\) for \(\kappa_D\).

symbols.name: Mbar
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound \(\overline M\) for \(M_H\).

symbols.name: CertificateInferenceHandle
symbols.def: Operator-norm affine-minor certification and chart-switching route defined in \(\text{def:certificate-inference-handle}\).
symbols.role: Concrete starting move for the open inference problem.

novel.justification: Strict positivity is an explicit interior restriction for the sharp replacement converse and quantitative conditioning. It holds whenever every structural disturbance coordinate has a nondegenerate invariant component, including latent-confounded systems with a full-rank background shock covariance.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}\ge0\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).
\(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

novel.justification: The prespecified-support factorization is a proposal-specific restriction that conditions on an investigator-chosen sparse intervention design. It is realistic in multi-environment experiments whose intervention targets are fixed before continuously distributed positive doses are assigned.

assumptions.condition: The joint law of \((a_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p,Z_{ek}=1)\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on its positive orthant.

novel.justification: Joint absolute continuity conditional on a fixed sparse support pattern is a genericity condition for nonzero intervention strengths. It is satisfied when active intervention variances have a joint density on the positive orthant, including independently randomized positive strengths and correlated continuously distributed dose designs.

definitions.name: Mkl
definitions.construction: For \(1\le k<\ell\le p\), \(M_{k\ell}=\max_{L\subset\mathbb R^2\,\mathrm{affine\ line}}\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

definitions.name: Rc
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{A\in\mathcal D:\exists K\subseteq E,\ |K|\ge h,\ \exists\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p,\ \exists t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,\ \Sigma_e=A^{-1}(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e))A^{-\mathsf T}\ \forall e\in K\}\).

definitions.name: gamma
definitions.construction: Set \(\gamma_H=0\) when \(h-c<3\); otherwise set \(\gamma_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}\end{pmatrix}\right|\).

definitions.name: SubsetConsensus
definitions.construction: Definitional implementation note: given a feasibility oracle that returns the full solution set for each queried semialgebraic system, query every \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\) for all \(A\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{offdiag}(A(\Sigma_e-\Sigma_f)A^{\mathsf T})=0\) for \(e,f\in K\) and admitting one \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p\) with nonnegative diagonal shifts for the transformed raw covariances. Define \(\text{SubsetConsensus}(\Sigma,c)\) as the union of the oracle-returned solution sets. This enumeration makes exactly \(\binom{m}{h}\) oracle queries and, by expansion of \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), its returned union equals \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\); neither fact is a theorem contribution or a claim that an encoded terminating solver is supplied.

definitions.name: rRadius
definitions.construction: \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\), where the supremum and hence the maximum may equal \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: diamOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\), \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A)=\sup_{A_1,A_2\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: outerOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\) and matrix \(D\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A,D)=\sup_{A_1\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: Ualpha
definitions.construction: For each \(n\ge1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}=\bigcup\{\mathcal R_c(\Gamma):\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in E\}\). On the simultaneous honest-slot coverage event \(\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\}\), take \(\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e\) for \(e\in H\) and choose an arbitrary point of the nonempty region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) for each \(e\in E\setminus H\); then \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\). Thus simultaneous honest-slot coverage of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) yields \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). If every region is the singleton \(\{\Sigma_e\}\) and \(\delta_H>c\), the sharp replacement-radius theorem gives the unlabeled sanity conclusion \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}=\{D\}\).

definitions.name: CertificateInferenceHandle
definitions.construction: Start from the finite subset enumeration in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\), represent noncollinearity without division by homogeneous \(3\times3\) affine minors, obtain operator-norm local perturbation control from the joint-diagonalization linearization indexed by \(\gamma_H,\kappa_D,\zeta_D,\lambda_H,M_H\), invert the indexed simultaneous covariance regions, and switch normalization charts only after forming chart-valid certificates.

statements.statement: Let the first explanation \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and the second explanation \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) fit the same \(\Sigma\), each through a BACKSHIFT covariance equation satisfying the unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization, with its own invariant positive-semidefinite nuisance, nonnegative shifts, and \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\). Set \(J=H_1\cap H_2\). Then \(|J|\ge m-2c=h-c\). If, for every \(k<\ell\), the first explanation's cloud \(\{(s^{(1)}_{ek},s^{(1)}_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) is not contained in an affine line, then \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\).
statements.justification: This isolates the new robust step: competing explanations share only \(m-2c\) slots, on which ordinary congruence-diagonalizer uniqueness must be normalized causally.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1, and KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, treat a fixed complete diagonalizable family rather than the intersection of two adversarially selected families.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the sufficiency half of the exact replacement-radius theorem after two candidate honest sets lose different slots.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\Psi^{(r)}\in\mathbb S_+^p\) denote the invariant nuisance in the \(r\)-th fitted BACKSHIFT equation.  Thus, by the fitting hypotheses in the statement,
\[
D^{(r)}\Sigma_eD^{(r)\mathsf T}
 =\Psi^{(r)}+\operatorname{diag}(s^{(r)}_e),
 \qquad e\in H_r.
\]
First, inclusion--exclusion and \(|E|=m\), \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\), give
\[
 |J|=|H_1\cap H_2|
 =|H_1|+|H_2|-|H_1\cup H_2|
 \ge 2h-m=m-2c=h-c.
\]

It remains to prove uniqueness.  Set \(Q=D^{(2)}(D^{(1)})^{-1}\).  The assumed noncollinearity implies that \(J\) is nonempty; fix \(e_0\in J\).  Subtracting the equation at \(e_0\) from the equation at \(e\in J\), and using the two displayed fits, yields
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q^{\mathsf T}
   =\operatorname{diag}(y_e),\qquad
 x_e=s^{(1)}_e-s^{(1)}_{e_0},\quad
 y_e=s^{(2)}_e-s^{(2)}_{e_0}.
\]
Let \(W=\operatorname{span}\{x_e:e\in J\}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\).  By linearity,
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(w)Q^{\mathsf T}\ \text{is diagonal for every }w\in W. \tag{1}
\]
For each \(k<\ell\), the coordinate projection of \(W\) onto coordinates \(k,\ell\) is all of \(\mathbb R^2\).  Indeed, if that projection had dimension at most one, some nonzero \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) would satisfy
\[
 a(s^{(1)}_{ek}-s^{(1)}_{e_0k})
 +b(s^{(1)}_{e\ell}-s^{(1)}_{e_0\ell})=0
 \quad\text{for every }e\in J,
\]
placing the entire \(k,\ell\) cloud in one affine line, contrary to the hypothesis.

Put \(d_W=\dim(W)\).  Choose a basis \(w^1,\ldots,w^{d_W}\) of \(W\), and define its \(k\)-th coordinate profile by
\[
 u_k=(w^1_k,\ldots,w^{d_W}_k)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d_W}.
\]
The preceding projection assertion says that \(u_k,u_\ell\) are linearly independent whenever \(k\ne\ell\).  In particular, every \(u_k\) is nonzero.  Choose \(\beta\in\mathbb R^{d_W}\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes \(\{\beta:\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k=0\}\).  Having chosen \(\beta\), choose \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^{d_W}\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes
\[
 \left\{\alpha:\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bigl((\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell)u_k-(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k)u_\ell\bigr)=0\right\},\qquad k<\ell.
\]
Every displayed normal vector is nonzero because \(u_k,u_\ell\) are linearly independent and both \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k\) and \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell\) are nonzero.  The choices exist because a finite union of proper linear hyperplanes cannot cover \(\mathbb R^{d_W}\): the product of their defining nonzero linear forms is a nonzero polynomial, while a nonzero real polynomial cannot vanish at every point (the latter follows by induction on the number of variables from the one-variable root bound).

Put
\[
 b=\sum_{q=1}^{d_W}\beta_qw^q,\qquad
 a=\sum_{q=1}^{d_W}\alpha_qw^q,\qquad
 \rho_k=\frac{a_k}{b_k}.
\]
The choice of \(\beta\) gives \(b_k\ne0\) for every \(k\), and the choice of \(\alpha\) gives \(\rho_k\ne\rho_\ell\) for \(k\ne\ell\).  By (1), both
\[
 G=Q\operatorname{diag}(a)Q^{\mathsf T}\quad\text{and}\quad
 K=Q\operatorname{diag}(b)Q^{\mathsf T}
\]
are diagonal.  Moreover, \(K\) is invertible because \(Q\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(b)\) are invertible.  Hence
\[
 GK^{-1}
 =Q\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_p)Q^{-1} \tag{2}
\]
is diagonal.  The eigenvalues on the right of (2) are pairwise distinct.  The eigenspaces of the diagonal matrix on the left are therefore the coordinate axes, so every column of \(Q\) is supported on exactly one coordinate.  Since \(Q\) is invertible, it is monomial: there are a permutation \(\pi\) and nonzero scalars \(q_i\) such that
\[
 Q_{i,\pi(i)}=q_i,\qquad Q_{ij}=0\quad(j\ne\pi(i)). \tag{3}
\]

It remains to remove the monomial ambiguity.  By \(\operatorname{diag}(D^{(1)})=\operatorname{diag}(D^{(2)})=\mathbf 1\), which is part of \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\), equations \(D^{(2)}=QD^{(1)}\) and (3) imply
\[
 1=D^{(2)}_{ii}=q_iD^{(1)}_{\pi(i),i}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(\pi\) had a nontrivial cycle \(i_1,\ldots,i_d\), with \(d\ge2\) and \(\pi(i_t)=i_{t+1}\) cyclically, then (4) would give
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^d\left|D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_t}\right|
 =\prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|^{-1}. \tag{5}
\]
The entries on the left of (5) form a directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(1)}\), while
\[
 D^{(2)}_{i_t,i_{t+1}}
 =q_{i_t}D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_{t+1}}=q_{i_t}
\]
form the reverse directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(2)}\).  The two strict cycle-product inequalities in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\) would consequently imply both
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|^{-1}<1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|<1,
\]
whose product is the contradiction \(1<1\).  Thus \(\pi\) is the identity.  Equation (4) and \(D^{(1)}_{ii}=1\) then give \(q_i=1\) for every \(i\).  Hence \(Q=I_p\) and \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\), as claimed.

statements.statement: Fix \(D,\Omega,H,s\) satisfying the honest BACKSHIFT model with \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), while the compatibility set permits positive-semidefinite invariant nuisances. The equality \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) holds for every assignment of arbitrary matrices from the positive-definite replacement domain to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\) if and only if \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\). If \(\delta_H\le c\), there exist positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that both \(D\) and \(D'\) belong to \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). At \(c=0\), the equivalence reduces to the BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity criterion.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact minimax number of whole environments that population BACKSHIFT can lose without losing the causal connectivity matrix.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift gives the \(c=0\) iff theorem, while AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD proposes threshold-based outlier omission; neither gives a worst-case replacement radius or a legal converse contamination. The robust joint-diagonalization literature informs the construction but is not treated as a theorem-level target.
statements.consumer: Investigators using heterogeneous biological or financial environments obtain an exact design audit before trusting a BACKSHIFT graph in the presence of corrupted regimes.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove sufficiency, the equivalence with the affine-minor margin, and necessity in turn.

Assume first that \(\delta_H>c\), and fix an arbitrary assignment of positive-definite matrices to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\).  By \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\), and \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), the choice \(K=H\), \(\Psi=\Omega\), and \(t_e=s_e\) in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\) shows that \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  Conversely, take any \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  By \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), there are \(K\subseteq E\), \(|K|\ge h\), \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\) such that \(A\) fits the BACKSHIFT covariance equation on \(K\).  The overlap \(J=H\cap K\) satisfies
\[
 |J|\ge |H|+|K|-m\ge2h-m=h-c. \tag{6}
\]
By \(\text{def:environment-distance}\) and \(\text{def:max-line-occupancy}\), \(\delta_H>c\) is equivalent to
\[
 M_{k\ell}<h-c\qquad\text{for every }k<\ell. \tag{7}
\]
If the honest \(k,\ell\) cloud restricted to \(J\) lay in an affine line, then (6) would imply \(M_{k\ell}\ge |J|\ge h-c\), contradicting (7).  Thus every pairwise cloud on \(J\) is noncollinear.  Applying \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\) to the explanations \((D,H,\Omega,s)\) and \((A,K,\Psi,t)\) gives \(A=D\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}. \tag{8}
\]
Nothing in this argument used the values assigned outside \(H\), so (8) holds for every allowed replacement assignment.

We next verify the asserted equivalence with \(\gamma_H\).  Put \(q=h-c\).  Any set of \(h\) points in \(\mathbb R^2\) has at least \(\min(2,h)\) points on an affine line, and hence
\[
 M_{k\ell}\ge\min(2,h). \tag{9}
\]
Consequently (7) is impossible when \(q<3\), exactly the regime in which \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) sets \(\gamma_H=0\).  Suppose now that \(q\ge3\).  For a fixed \(S\subseteq H\), \(|S|=q\), and fixed \(k<\ell\), all determinants
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\
 1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\
 1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}
 \end{pmatrix},\qquad e<f<g,\quad e,f,g\in S, \tag{10}
\]
vanish if and only if the matrix with rows \((1,s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\), \(e\in S\), has rank at most two, which is equivalent to the \(k,\ell\) points indexed by \(S\) lying in one affine line.  Thus the inner maximum in \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) is positive exactly when \(S\) is not contained in an affine line.  There are finitely many pairs and subsets, so their minimum is positive exactly when no affine line contains \(q\) honest points for any pair.  Therefore
\[
 \gamma_H>0
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ M_{k\ell}<q\ \text{for all }k<\ell
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \delta_H>c. \tag{11}
\]

For necessity, suppose \(\delta_H\le c\).  We construct one legal replacement assignment having a second compatible structural matrix.  Again write \(q=h-c=m-2c\).

If \(q\le0\), then \(c\ge h\), so \(E\setminus H\) contains a subset \(H'\) of size \(h\).  Fix \(k\ne\ell\), and let \(E_{k\ell}\) be the matrix with a one in position \(k,\ell\) and zeros elsewhere.  For all sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\),
\[
 D'=D+\varepsilon E_{k\ell}
\]
has unit diagonal, is invertible, and satisfies \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D')<1\): invertibility and the strict cycle-product inequality persist by continuity from \(\varepsilon=0\).  Hence \(D'\in\mathcal D\) and \(D'\ne D\).  Set \(\Omega'=I_p\), and assign
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T},\qquad e\in E\setminus H.
\]
These matrices are positive definite.  The original \(D\) fits the \(h\) slots in \(H\), while \(D'\) fits the \(h\) slots in \(H'\) with zero shifts.  Thus both matrices belong to \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).

It remains to treat \(q>0\).  By \(\delta_H\le c\), there are \(k<\ell\), an affine line \(L\), and a subset \(S\subseteq H\) of size \(q\) whose \(k,\ell\) shift points lie on \(L\).  Choose a nonzero direction \(v=(v_k,v_\ell)\) for \(L\), fix \(e_0\in S\), and write
\[
 (s_{ek}-s_{e_0k},s_{e\ell}-s_{e_0\ell})=\tau_e(v_k,v_\ell),\qquad e\in S. \tag{12}
\]
For a scalar \(\varepsilon\), define
\[
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)=1+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k},\qquad
 \eta_\ell(\varepsilon)=1-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell},
\]
and let \(Q_\varepsilon\) be the identity outside rows and columns \(k,\ell\), with \(k,\ell\) block
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\varepsilon v_k\eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}\\
 -\varepsilon v_\ell\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{13}
\]
For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), both denominators and \(Q_\varepsilon\) are invertible.  Put \(D'_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon D\).  The two changed diagonal entries are
\[
 (D'_\varepsilon)_{kk}
 =\frac{D_{kk}+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k}}{\eta_k(\varepsilon)}=1,\qquad
 (D'_\varepsilon)_{\ell\ell}
 =\frac{D_{\ell\ell}-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell}}{\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=1, \tag{14}
\]
and the other diagonal entries remain one.  Since \(Q_0=I_p\), the strict inequality \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)<1\) and invertibility persist by continuity.  Because \(v\ne0\), every sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\) also has \(Q_\varepsilon\ne I_p\).  Hence we may choose a nonzero \(\varepsilon\) such that
\[
 D'=D'_\varepsilon\in\mathcal D,\qquad D'\ne D. \tag{15}
\]

For \(x_e=s_e-s_{e_0}\), equations (12)--(13) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 [Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{k\ell}
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell x_{ek}+\varepsilon v_kx_{e\ell}}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}\\
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell\tau_ev_k+\varepsilon v_k\tau_ev_\ell}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=0.
 \end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
All other off-diagonal entries in (16) vanish because \(Q_\varepsilon\) differs from the identity only in the \(k,\ell\) block.  Define \(\operatorname{off}(G)=G-\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{diag}(G))\).  Equation (16) shows that
\[
 C_\varepsilon
 =\operatorname{off}\!\left(Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\right)
\]
does not depend on \(e\in S\).  Set
\[
 \Omega'_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon\Omega Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}+C_\varepsilon. \tag{17}
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), \(C_0=0\) and \(\Omega'_0=\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\) by \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\).  Positive definiteness is open, so the nonzero \(\varepsilon\) in (15) may be chosen still smaller so that
\[
 \Omega'=\Omega'_\varepsilon\in\mathbb S_{++}^p. \tag{18}
\]
For \(e\in S\), define
\[
 t_{ei}=[Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{ii}
 =\sum_{j=1}^p(Q_\varepsilon)_{ij}^2s_{ej}\ge0, \tag{19}
\]
where the inequality uses \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\).  Equations (17)--(19) imply, for every \(e\in S\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D'\Sigma_eD'^{\mathsf T}
 &=Q_\varepsilon(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e))Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=\Omega'+\operatorname{diag}(t_e).
 \end{aligned} \tag{20}
\]
Now set \(H'=S\cup(E\setminus H)\), which has size \(q+c=h\), and assign every replaced slot the positive-definite covariance
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T},\qquad e\in E\setminus H. \tag{21}
\]
Equations (20)--(21) show that \(D'\) fits all of \(H'\), using shifts \(t_e\) on \(S\) and zero shifts outside \(H\).  The original \(D\) continues to fit \(H\).  Thus \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\), while \(D'\ne D\), and (18), (19), and (21) give precisely the required positive-definite nuisance, nonnegative shifts, and positive-definite replacements.

As an exact check of the smallest nontrivial ambiguity, take \(p=2\), \(m=3\), \(c=1\), \(D=I_2\), \(\Omega=I_2\), \(H=\{1,2\}\), \(s_1=(0,0)\), and \(s_2=(1,1)\).  Put \(\Sigma_1=I_2\), \(\Sigma_2=2I_2\), and replace the third slot by \(\Sigma_3=I_2\).  For \(0<|\varepsilon|<1\),
\[
 D'=\begin{pmatrix}1&\varepsilon\\-\varepsilon&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \Omega'=(1+\varepsilon^2)I_2
\]
satisfy \(\operatorname{CP}(I_2-D')=\varepsilon^2<1\).  Moreover, \(D'\Sigma_eD'^{\mathsf T}=\Omega'\) for \(e=1,3\), and
\[
 D'\Sigma_2D'^{\mathsf T}
 =\Omega'+\operatorname{diag}(1+\varepsilon^2,1+\varepsilon^2).
\]
Thus the ambiguity is literal, not a boundary limit.

Finally, if \(c=0\), then \(h=m\) and
\[
 \delta_H>0
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ M_{k\ell}<h\ \text{for every }k<\ell,
\]
which says exactly that no full pairwise shift cloud is contained in an affine line.  This is the stated BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity specialization.

statements.statement: Under the prespecified support pattern \(Z\) and absolutely continuous active amplitudes, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), \(M_{k\ell}=M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) almost surely. Consequently, corruption-robust identification holds almost surely if and only if, for every \(k<\ell\), \(\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}<h-c\). In particular, any robustly identifying support pattern satisfies \(m\ge2c+3\), and this environment-count lower bound is attained by support patterns with no larger forced affine incidence.
statements.justification: The closed formula converts an unobservable general-position condition into an exact support-hypergraph design threshold and exposes the unavoidable \(2c+3\) environment floor.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Corollary 2(ii), treats fully continuous intervention variances, and PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 5.3, and Corollary 5.4, studies sparse mechanism changes without affine-line occupancy or adversarial slot replacement.
statements.consumer: Experimental planners can choose which variables to shift in each environment so the resulting sparse design tolerates a prespecified number of failed environments.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k<\ell\), and write
\[
 P_e=(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})=(Z_{ek}a_{ek},Z_{e\ell}a_{e\ell}),\qquad e\in H.
\]
The four support types \(00,10,01,11\) place \(P_e\), respectively, at the origin, on the positive horizontal axis, on the positive vertical axis, and in the open positive quadrant.

We first identify all incidences forced by the support pattern.  The horizontal axis contains exactly \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell}\) indexed points, the vertical axis contains exactly \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell}\), and, if \(n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\), the line through the origin and any one \(11\) point contains \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+1\) indexed points.  Finally, an affine line contains any prescribed two points, counting distinct environment indices even when the two points coincide.  Hence, deterministically,
\[
 M_{k\ell}\ge
 \max\!\left\{
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,h)
 \right\}. \tag{22}
\]

We now show that no other incidence occurs outside a Lebesgue-null set of active amplitudes.  For two nonzero-support points \(P_e=(x_e,y_e)\) and \(P_f=(x_f,y_f)\), collinearity with the origin is the polynomial equation
\[
 x_ey_f-x_fy_e=0. \tag{23}
\]
Unless both support types are \(10\), or both are \(01\), the polynomial in (23) is nonzero: for the mixed types \(10,01\), \(10,11\), and \(01,11\), it contains a nonzero product of positive active coordinates, while for two \(11\) points it is \(x_ey_f-x_fy_e\) with two distinct monomials.  Likewise, for three nonzero-support points, collinearity is the polynomial equation
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 1&x_e&y_e\\1&x_f&y_f\\1&x_g&y_g
 \end{pmatrix}=0. \tag{24}
\]
Except when all three types are \(10\), or all three are \(01\), the polynomial in (24) is not identically zero.  This can be checked within each support type without leaving the positive orthant: two horizontal points and a vertical or \(11\) point can be chosen noncollinear; the analogous assertion holds with the axes exchanged; one point of each relevant mixed type can be chosen off the line through the other two; and three \(11\) points may be chosen as \((1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\).  We also exclude equality of the active coordinates of two distinct \(10\) points and, analogously, of two distinct \(01\) points; each is the zero set of a nonzero linear polynomial.

For completeness, the zero set of a nonzero polynomial in finitely many real variables has Lebesgue measure zero.  This follows by induction on the number of variables: in one variable there are finitely many roots; in the induction step, write the polynomial as a polynomial in the last variable, choose one nonzero coefficient polynomial, use the induction hypothesis on the zero set of that coefficient, and observe that every remaining one-dimensional section has finitely many roots.  Integrating these null sections gives a null set.  There are only finitely many equality, pair, triple, and coordinate-pair events above.  The joint absolute continuity in \(\text{ass:generic-active-amplitudes}\) consequently implies that, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), none of these accidental equations occurs almost surely.

On this probability-one event, let \(L\) be an affine line.  If \(L\) passes through the origin and contains a \(10\) point, then \(L\) is the horizontal axis and has occupancy \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell}\).  The corresponding conclusion for a \(01\) point gives the vertical-axis term.  If it contains neither axis type, (23) permits at most one \(11\) point, giving occupancy at most \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\}\).  If \(L\) does not pass through the origin, it contains no \(00\) point.  Were it to contain three indexed points, (24) would force all three to be \(10\) or all three to be \(01\); but their line would then be an axis and would pass through the origin, a contradiction.  Such a line therefore has occupancy at most \(\min(2,h)\).  Combining these upper bounds with (22) proves
\[
 M_{k\ell}
 =\max\!\left\{
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,h)
 \right\}
 =M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{25}
\]
The exceptional set was chosen as a finite union over all \(k<\ell\), so (25) holds simultaneously for every pair.

By \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) and \(\text{def:environment-distance}\), robust identification is equivalent to
\[
 \delta_H>c
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ h-M_{k\ell}>c\ \text{for every }k<\ell
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ M_{k\ell}<h-c\ \text{for every }k<\ell. \tag{26}
\]
Substitution of (25) into (26) gives exactly the four-term support criterion in the statement.

Because the fourth term in (25) is \(\min(2,h)\), the strict inequality in (26) requires \(h-c\ge3\).  Since \(h=m-c\), this is
\[
 m\ge2c+3. \tag{27}
\]
The bound is attained.  For any \(c\ge0\), take \(m=2c+3\), so \(h=c+3\), and choose the all-active pattern \(Z_{ek}=1\) for every \(e,k\).  Then for every \(k<\ell\),
\[
 n_{11}^{k\ell}=h,\qquad
 n_{00}^{k\ell}=n_{10}^{k\ell}=n_{01}^{k\ell}=0,\qquad
 M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=2<h-c=3.
\]
Thus this pattern has the smallest possible forced affine occupancy and robustly identifies almost surely at equality in (27), completing the proof.

statements.statement:
The definition-level coverage claim is valid, but the requested computable confidence-union construction has a negative answer for the region class stated in the question.  More precisely, if
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
then \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\), and consequently \(\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\ge 1-\alpha\) implies \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\ge1-\alpha\).

For a rational population covariance family \(\Sigma\), the population compatibility set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) has an exact rational semialgebraic description.  Effective real quantifier elimination therefore supplies finite rational-polynomial certificates for infeasibility, singleton output, and multiple-candidate output.  The affine minors of the fitted diagonal shifts can be included, without division, among the sign polynomials in each certificate.  These minors certify separation, but they cannot by themselves certify feasibility: the covariance equations, positive-semidefinite invariant nuisance, nonnegative shifts, invertibility, unit diagonal, and cycle-product inequalities are also necessary.  Normalization-chart changes are sound when pivot nonvanishing and all normalization and cycle inequalities are cleared to polynomial sign conditions before a chart certificate is accepted.

In contrast, when \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) is only an arbitrary nonempty subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\), as in the frozen definition, no deterministic procedure making only finitely many membership queries to these sets can return the exact full set \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) for every region family.  This failure already occurs for \(p=2\), \(m=3\), and \(c=0\), with rational positive-definite matrices and a design having affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H=1\).  Hence the complete conjunction requested in the open question is false as stated: an exact computable confidence union, and thus a computable full-output-or-abstain rule at \(\gamma_H=0\), requires an additional effective representation of the regions.  The causal target remains \(B=I_p-D\); neither the coverage inclusion nor the semialgebraic description defines that target to equal an observable functional.
statements.proof_tex:
We separate the coverage statement, the rational population calculation, and the computational obstruction.

\emph{Coverage.}  Fix \(n\ge1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  On \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\), set \(\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e\) for \(e\in H\).  For each \(e\in E\setminus H\), choose any \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\); this is possible because every indexed region is nonempty.  By \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\), \(D\in\mathcal D\).  By \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\), \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\subseteq\mathbb S_+^p\).  By \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), \(s_e\in[0,\infty)^p\) for \(e\in H\), and by \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\),
\[
\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e=D^{-1}\{\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\}D^{-\mathsf T},\qquad e\in H.
\]
Since \(|H|=h\), the witnesses \(K=H\), \(A=D\), \(\Psi=\Omega\), and \(t_e=s_e\) meet every condition in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).  Thus \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\).  The union in \(\text{def:confidence-union}\) contains this choice of \(\Gamma\), so
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}.
\]
Monotonicity of probability now gives
\[
\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\ge \Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This proves coverage without equating the causal matrix \(D\), or \(B=I_p-D\), with the random set \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\).

\emph{Exact rational population certificates.}  Suppose every entry of every \(\Sigma_e\) is rational.  It is enough to enumerate subsets \(K\subseteq E\) having \(|K|=h\): any witness with more than \(h\) slots restricts to one with exactly \(h\) slots.  For such a \(K\), let \(\mathcal F_K(A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K})\) be the following finite conjunction:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&A_{ii}=1 &&(1\le i\le p),\\
&(\det A)^2>0,\\
&\prod_{(i,j)\in C}A_{ij}^2<1
&&\text{for every directed simple cycle \(C\) of length at least two},\\
&\Psi=\Psi^{\mathsf T},\qquad x^{\mathsf T}\Psi x\ge0
&&\text{for every \(x\in\mathbb R^p\)},\\
&t_{ek}\ge0 &&(e\in K,\ 1\le k\le p),\\
&A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e) &&(e\in K).
\end{aligned}
\]
The universally quantified inequality in the fourth line is the definition of \(\Psi\succeq0\).  For an off-diagonal entry, \((I_p-A)_{ij}=-A_{ij}\); hence the finitely many cycle inequalities are equivalent to \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)<1\).  It follows directly from \(\text{def:compatible-set}\) that
\[
A\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\ \mathcal F_K(A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K}).
\tag{1}
\]
All polynomials in (1), including those under the universal quantifier defining positive semidefiniteness, have rational coefficients.  Define the right-hand side of (1) to be \(\mathcal F(A)\).  The three output cases are expressed by the closed first-order formulas
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{infeasible:}&\neg\exists A\,\mathcal F(A),\\[2mm]
\text{singleton:}&\exists A\,[\mathcal F(A)\wedge
 \forall A'\{\mathcal F(A')\Rightarrow\sum_{i,j}(A'_{ij}-A_{ij})^2=0\}],\\[2mm]
\text{multiple:}&\exists A\,\exists A'\,[\mathcal F(A)\wedge\mathcal F(A')
 \wedge\sum_{i,j}(A'_{ij}-A_{ij})^2>0].
\end{array}
\tag{2}
\]
They are exhaustive because a nonempty set either has exactly one element or contains two distinct elements.  Applying \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) to (1) gives a quantifier-free rational semialgebraic description of the full set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\), and applying it to (2) decides the three cases.  The resulting finite Boolean combination of rational polynomial sign conditions is the exact symbolic certificate; in each closed case of (2), its remaining signs are signs of rational constants and are checked exactly.

For every \(e,f,g\in K\) and \(k<\ell\), adjoin the polynomial
\[
q_{efg;k\ell}(t)=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix}
\tag{3}
\]
to the sign family.  It has integer coefficients and is homogeneous with respect to the determinant calculation, so no ratio is taken.  The signs of (3) record precisely the affine-minor separation of each fitted shift cloud.  Formula (1) shows why these signs alone are not feasibility certificates: none of invertibility, positive semidefiniteness, nonnegative shifts, or the covariance equations follows from (3).

No normalization chart is needed in (1), because unit diagonal and all cycle products are imposed globally.  If a row-permutation calculation is used internally, let \(u_i\ne0\) denote the pivot used to normalize row \(i\).  Replace every division by \(u_i\) with its cross-multiplied polynomial equality, retain the sign condition \(u_i^2>0\), and multiply every rational cycle inequality by the positive product of the relevant \(u_i^2\).  These operations are equivalences on that chart.  There are finitely many row permutations and pivot choices, and a proposed candidate is accepted only after satisfying (1); consequently switching among these certified charts cannot change the returned set.

\emph{Why arbitrary set-valued regions are not computable inputs.}  We give an explicit finite-query indistinguishability witness.  Take \(p=2\), \(m=h=3\), \(c=0\), \(H=E\),
\[
D=I_2,\qquad \Omega=I_2,\qquad
s_1=(0,0),\quad s_2=(1,0),\quad s_3=(0,1).
\]
Then
\[
\Sigma_1=I_2,\qquad \Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,1),\qquad
\Sigma_3=\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
\]
and the unique affine minor is
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}=1,
\]
so \(\gamma_H=1\).  Let \(\mathcal C^0_e=\{\Sigma_e\}\).  We first verify directly that \(\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)=\{I_2\}\).  If \(A\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)\), unit diagonal gives
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\b&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Subtracting the fitted covariance equations between environments 2 and 1 makes the invariant nuisance cancel and gives a diagonal matrix on the right.  Its off-diagonal entry on the left is
\[
\left[A\operatorname{diag}(1,0)A^{\mathsf T}\right]_{12}=b,
\]
so \(b=0\).  Similarly, environments 3 and 1 give
\[
\left[A\operatorname{diag}(0,1)A^{\mathsf T}\right]_{12}=a,
\]
so \(a=0\).  Hence \(A=I_2\), while the displayed \(D,\Omega,s\) show that \(I_2\) is feasible.  Therefore the confidence union formed from \(\mathcal C^0\) is \(\{I_2\}\).

For a nonzero rational number \(q\), put
\[
A_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Gamma_e(q)=A_q^{-1}\{I_2+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\}A_q^{-\mathsf T}.
\]
Every \(\Gamma_e(q)\) is rational and positive definite.  Moreover, \(A_q\) has unit diagonal, is invertible, and \(\operatorname{CP}(I_2-A_q)=0<1\).  Thus \(A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Gamma(q))\), witnessed by invariant nuisance \(I_2\) and the displayed nonnegative shifts.

Consider any deterministic purported exact algorithm which is allowed finitely many adaptive membership questions of the form ``is \(Q\in\mathcal C_e\)?'' and then halts.  Run it on \(\mathcal C^0\); only finitely many matrices \(Q\) are queried.  For each fixed queried \(Q\) and environment \(e\), the equality \(Q=\Gamma_e(q)\) excludes at most one \(q\), because
\[
[\Gamma_e(q)]_{12}=-q(1+s_{e2})
\]
and \(1+s_{e2}>0\).  Choose a nonzero rational \(q\) outside this finite exceptional set and define
\[
\mathcal C^1_e=\{\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e(q)\},\qquad e=1,2,3.
\]
Every membership answer along the run is identical for \(\mathcal C^0\) and \(\mathcal C^1\), so determinism forces the same output.  But selecting \(\Sigma_e\) in every slot shows \(I_2\in\mathcal U(\mathcal C^1)\), while selecting \(\Gamma_e(q)\) in every slot shows \(A_q\in\mathcal U(\mathcal C^1)\).  Since \(q\ne0\),
\[
\mathcal U(\mathcal C^0)=\{I_2\}\ne\mathcal U(\mathcal C^1).
\]
This contradiction proves the finite-query impossibility.  The frozen type of \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_\alpha\) supplies not even a membership oracle, much less a finite semialgebraic encoding, so an exact computable implementation cannot be asserted on that type.  Likewise, detecting that some compatible explanation has \(\gamma_H=0\) cannot be required computationally without an effective input representation.  Set-theoretically one may always return the full union or abstain; effectivity is the missing premise.

Thus the coverage implication and the rational population certificate are established, while the conjunction demanded by the question is false under the declared arbitrary-region input class.  This obstruction is computational and does not by itself affirm or refute a separate analytic local-modulus claim for \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}\), or \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}\) after an effective region class is specified.
statements.justification: This gives the exact definition-level coverage proof, an executable symbolic population certificate for rational covariances, and an explicit witness showing why exact confidence-union computation is impossible for the frozen arbitrary-set region type.
statements.gap: The result isolates input representation as a logically prior obstruction. It leaves the analytic local-modulus problem separate rather than silently assuming a finite encoding of arbitrary confidence regions.
statements.consumer: An implementation may use the rational semialgebraic population certificate immediately, but must require an effective region representation before promising exact confidence unions or boundary-triggered abstention.

statements.statement: Every first-order formula over the ordered field of real numbers whose atomic predicates are sign conditions on finitely many polynomials with rational coefficients admits an effectively computable equivalent quantifier-free formula.  In particular, closed such formulas are decidable, and projections of rational semialgebraic sets have computable rational semialgebraic descriptions.

source.locator: Section 2, especially the Tarski--Seidenberg theorem and the effective quantifier-elimination theorem labeled 14:the:tqe in the source

attestation.note: Checked against Saugata Basu, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry: A Survey, arXiv:1409.1534, Section 2; the stable arXiv handle is supplied in lieu of a long verbatim transcription.

sampling_model.design: There are \(m\) labeled environments; an unknown set \(H\) of size \(h=m-c\) follows one population BACKSHIFT covariance model and the remaining \(c\) slots are arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).
sampling_model.units: For population identification only \(\Sigma_e\) is observed. At each index \(n\), every slot supplies an independent within-environment sample of size \(n\) used to construct the indexed simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown additive shift interventions have diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\); intervention targets and strengths are not observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The two candidate honest subsets may overlap in only \(m-2c=h-c\) slots.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated for the population theorem. Compatibility permits an invariant nuisance in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); the sharp converse and conditioning analysis impose the explicit interior condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\). The inference layer propagates indexed honest-slot simultaneous covariance regions through feasibility-oracle constraint inversion and measures all perturbations in operator norm.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The population BACKSHIFT solution is unique exactly when every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
An exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer is essentially unique if and only if the diagonal-profile collinearity modulus is below one.
Outlier target matrices are omitted by iteratively retaining matrices whose geometric residual is below a chosen threshold.

Theorem 1 gives noiseless unique topology identification when the exogenous-covariance factor has Kruskal rank at least two, nonzero edges are continuously distributed, and at least two off-diagonal nonzero entries are known in every column.
Simultaneous diagonalizability by congruence of a complete Hermitian family is equivalent to positive-definite feasibility of a linear matrix system.
Pairwise environment comparisons identify causal structure with high probability under probabilistically sparse mechanism changes.
Identification-robust tests and confidence sets maintain uniform asymptotic size across weak and strong identification regimes.

tldr: Unknown shift interventions identify a cyclic linear causal system because covariance differences share a non-unitary congruence diagonalizer. The field-tier kernel asks how many entire covariance environments may instead be arbitrary. The structural matrix satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization survives every \(c\)-slot positive-definite replacement if and only if deleting the largest affine-line subset from every pairwise honest shift cloud costs more than \(c\) environments. The converse uses the explicit interior condition on invariant noise to produce a legal positive-definite contamination and a second cycle-product-normalized system. A generic sparse-support formula turns the distance into a combinatorial design criterion; finite subset enumeration is only a reduction to an exact feasibility oracle, while operator-norm contraction of indexed confidence unions, rational certificates, and mandatory abstention at zero affine separation remain the computational agenda for updating the CRAN pooled-difference workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published BACKSHIFT identifies from an entirely honest environment family, general joint-diagonalization theory studies one complete matrix family, and existing outlier-aware joint diagonalization uses a tuning threshold without an exact adversarial radius.
project_justification.niche: Whole-environment replacement creates a discrete overlap geometry: two explanations may discard different slots and therefore share only \(m-2c\) covariance matrices. Affine rather than linear collinearity is the invariant obstruction because the common nondiagonal noise covariance disappears only after differencing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the necessary-and-sufficient distance \(\delta_H>c\), a matching positive-definite contamination witness satisfying the BACKSHIFT cycle-product normalization under the interior-noise condition, and the exact generic support-incidence formula. Finite subset enumeration is recorded only as a definitional feasibility-oracle implementation note. The open inference target asks for explicit operator-norm radius and modulus functions for indexed confidence unions on fixed-margin uniform classes, rational certificates, chart switching, and abstention at vanishing affine minors.

related_work: The field-tier radius result is informed by RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and its appendix proof, which supplies the all-honest model, pairwise profile reduction, and cycle-product normalization; its generic-amplitude result is Corollary 2(ii). KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, informs the complete-family uniqueness step through profile collinearity. AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD, Section 4.2 and equation (42), informs the robust joint-diagonalization setting by trimming outlier target matrices with a chosen residual threshold, but it does not state a worst-case replacement radius. ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM, Section III.C and equations (27)--(28), defines R-JDSEM through an elementwise \(\ell_1\) joint-diagonalization loss for sparse node- or entry-level outlier components within local covariance matrices, rather than replacement of whole covariance slabs. Its noiseless anchored or known-edge Theorem 1 establishes a sufficient uniqueness result under prior edge information; it gives neither an adversarial whole-environment replacement radius, the criterion \(\delta_H>c\), nor a legal two-explanation BACKSHIFT converse. PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 5.3, and Corollary 5.4, shows how pairwise environment comparisons and sparse mechanism changes support detection and graph recovery, while PfisterPeters2022SparseIV, Theorem 3, illustrates how a support pattern can control generic causal identifiability. LeNguyen2022HermitianSDC, Theorem 7 and Algorithm 5, supplies a complete-family congruence-feasibility primitive; this proposal uses it only to motivate an oracle reduction and does not claim a terminating exact solver. Afsari2008JDSensitivity relates local joint-diagonalization error to conditioning and a uniqueness modulus. AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID motivates confidence procedures that remain valid as identification disappears. None of these sources characterizes adversarial positive-definite replacement of covariance environments under BACKSHIFT normalization and nonnegative raw shifts.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(p=2,c=1,m=3\) ambiguity check uses \(D=I_2\), \(D'=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(\Sigma_1=I_2\), \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)\), and \(\Sigma_3=I_2+D'^{-1}D'^{-\mathsf T}\). Both explanations fit two slots, \(\operatorname{CP}(I_2-D')=1/4\), and \(\Sigma_3\) has positive principal minors \(29/9\) and \(65/9\). This diagnostic is not itself a contribution and does not establish the general converse.
honest_scope: The exact population radius and generic sparse-support frontier are theorem targets. The invariant nuisance is positive semidefinite in the standard BACKSHIFT layer and is required to be positive definite only for the sharp converse, the raw-covariance \(c=0\) reduction, and conditioning claims. Finite subset enumeration is a definitional reduction to a full-solution feasibility oracle, not an encoded solver. The rational certificate atlas, implementable feasibility routine, normalization-chart switching, and operator-norm contraction of \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) remain the first-class open question. Contraction is requested only along indexed region sequences with \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), uniformly on classes bounded away from zero affine separation, normalization slack, and positive-definiteness margins and bounded above in condition number and scale; at \(\gamma_H=0\), set-valued output or abstention remains mandatory. At \(c=0\), the positive-definite raw-covariance criterion is explicitly a non-novel reduction to the published BACKSHIFT noncollinearity result; no statistical rate is claimed without explicit covariance-region inputs.
